# svdx
The package implements **Smoothing Spline Analysis of Variance–Singular Value Decomposition** (SSANOVA-SVD) for system-level modeling of high-dimensional data. It reconstructs overarching processes as smooth functions of observed covariates and estimates feature loadings describing their contributions to the measurements.

The resulting system-level models can be used within the three-step analytical framework encompassing process reconstruction, out-of-sample prediction, and conditional inference of feature participation. The example below illustrates these steps.

This README focuses on the **single-dataset svdx()** interface. Documentation for other methods implemented in the package will accompany forthcoming manuscripts.

## Requirements

- R (>= 4.1.0) and a working C++ toolchain for compiling R packages.
- [NLopt](https://nlopt.readthedocs.io/) installed as a system library and discoverable with `pkg-config`.
- R package dependencies declared in `DESCRIPTION`, including `Rcpp`, `RcppArmadillo`, and `RcppParallel`.

The package uses TBB for parallel computation. The build links against the TBB libraries provided by **RcppParallel**; a separate Homebrew TBB installation is not expected to be necessary on macOS. This configuration has been inspected on Apple Silicon macOS; other platforms have not yet been verified.

### macOS (Homebrew)

Install NLopt and `pkg-config`:

```sh
brew install nlopt pkg-config
```

Then, in R:

```r
install.packages(c("Rcpp", "RcppArmadillo", "RcppParallel", "remotes"))
remotes::install_github("mskb01/svdx", dependencies = TRUE)
library(svdx)
```

Replace `mskb01/svdx` with the repository location once published.

### Ubuntu/Debian

Install the NLopt development headers, `pkg-config`, and the tools needed to compile R packages:

```sh
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install libnlopt-dev pkg-config build-essential
```

Then install the R dependencies and package as above. Linux installation has not yet been tested for this release.

**Note:** The package's `configure` script uses `pkg-config` to locate NLopt. If NLopt is installed in a nonstandard location, configure `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` before installation. The package has not been built or tested on Windows.

## Model

For a feature-by-sample matrix $Y \in \mathbb{R}^{p \times n}$, the model represents the measurements using a low-rank component and optional adjustment effects:

$$
Y \approx VU^\top + Z\zeta,
$$

where $U \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times K}$ contains sample-level processes modeled as smooth functions of study covariates, and $V \in \mathbb{R}^{p \times K}$ contains feature loadings. Optional nuisance covariates are specified separately.

## Basic usage

The following illustrates the **non-family (Gaussian) `svdx()` interface**. `Y` must have features in rows and samples in columns; `data` must have one row per sample, in the same order as the columns of `Y`.


```r
library(svdx)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(limma)

#Generate data 
set.seed(1)
n <- 100
p <- 500
sample_data <- data.frame(
  time = rep(seq(0, 1, length.out = n/2),2),
  group = factor(rep(c("A", "B"), each = n/2))
)

Y0 <- matrix(rnorm(p * n), nrow = p, ncol = n) 
tprof <- cos(sample_data$time*2*pi)
Yt <- 0*Y0
Yt[ 1:4, ] <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq(4), function(x) tprof) )
signs <- c(1,-1,1,-1)
Yt[1:4,] <- sweep( Yt[1:4,], 1, signs, "*" )

mu <- c(-1, 2)
b <- c(model.matrix( ~sample_data$group ) %*% mu)
Yb <- 0*Y0
scales <- c(1, .25, .25, 1)
Yb[5:8,] <- do.call( rbind, lapply( seq(4), function(x) c(b)*scales[x] ) )
cbio <- 2
Y <- Y0 + cbio*(Yt + Yb)

rownames(Y) <- paste0("feature_", seq_len(p))
colnames(Y) <- paste0("sample_", seq_len(n))
rownames(sample_data) <- colnames(Y)

# Data split 
train <- sample( n, .7*n )
test <- seq(n)[-train]
Ytrain <- Y[,train]
sample_data_train <- sample_data[train,]
Ytest <- Y[,test]
sample_data_test <- sample_data[test,]

#Step 1: Fit ssanova-svd for the train data
fit <- svdx(
  Y = Ytrain,
  K = 3,
  formula = ~ group + time,
  data = sample_data_train,
  zformula = ~ 1,
  zdata = sample_data_train,
  modelType = list(time = list("cubic", range(sample_data$time))), #range should be specified 
  family = NULL,
  est_K = TRUE,
  numThreads = 2
)

#Visualize and interpret
g1 <- data.frame( sample_data, groupEffect=cbio*b, timeEffect=cbio*tprof ) |> 
  tidyr::pivot_longer( cols = c(groupEffect, timeEffect) ) |> 
  ggplot( aes( x= time, y=value, group = group, color=group) ) + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name) + theme_bw()
  
c1 <-plotU(fit, data = sample_data, component = 1, x = "time", group="group")
c2 <- plotU(fit, data = sample_data, component = 2, x = "time", group="group") 
g1/(c1+c2)

#Step 2: predict processes in external data without using their measurements
pred <- predict( fit, newdata = sample_data_test  ) 

#Step 3: conditional inference using unused measurements
design <- model.matrix( ~pred ) 
lmfit <- lmFit( Ytest, design)
eb <- eBayes(lmfit)
which(p.adjust(eb$p.value[,2], "BH") < .1) #features participating in the first process
which(p.adjust(eb$p.value[,3], "BH") < .1) #features participating in the second process
#omnibus F tests can also be made using the limma interface 
```

### Core arguments

| Argument | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `Y` | Numeric feature-by-sample matrix. |
| `K` | Maximum number of components to fit. |
| `formula`, `data` | Study covariates used to model component functions. |
| `zformula`, `zdata` | Optional nuisance/adjustment covariates. |
| `modelType` | Basis/model specification for covariates, where needed. |
| `family` | `NULL` for the non-family Gaussian workflow documented here. |
| `est_K` | Whether to estimate the number of components. |
| `nfolds` | Number of cross-validation folds (default: 5). |
| `numThreads` | Number of parallel worker threads. |
| `fitter_control`, `optCV_control`, `nlopt_control` | Optional numerical optimization controls. |

See `?svdx` for the full argument list, including offsets, basis selection, and graph-related options.

## Fitted components and prediction

The returned object has class `SSANOVASVD`. Its fitted results include component scores, feature loadings, and adjustment estimates. For the current result structure, these are available under `fit$fitAtOptCV`:

```r
U <- fit$fitAtOptCV$umat
V <- fit$fitAtOptCV$vmat
```

Sample-level process functions can be evaluated at covariate values using the package's prediction method:

```r
pred <- predict(fit, newdata = sample_data_train)
```

The same interface can be used to decompose each component in terms of covariate contributions
```r
pred_group <- predict(fit, newdata = sample_data_train, include="group")
pred_time <- predict(fit, newdata = sample_data_train, include="time")
```

For usage and available prediction options, see `?predict.SSANOVASVD`.

## Documentation and reproducibility

```r
?svdx
?predict.SSANOVASVD
```

Analysis scripts reproducing the manuscript's simulations and applications will be provided separately in `svdxAnalysis`.

## Troubleshooting and numerical warnings

**NLopt round-off errors.** On rare occasions, NLopt may terminate with a
round-off error due to numerical limitations. If this occurs, relaxing the
optimization tolerances (i.e., using less stringent convergence criteria `ftol_abs`, 
`xtol_abs`) may resolve the issue.

**Convergence warnings during hyperparameter optimization.** During
hyperparameter optimization, convergence warnings may occasionally be
reported for candidate hyperparameter settings. These warnings can
generally be ignored, provided the overall optimization completes
successfully.
